ink-faint.contrastNote: 4.75:1 vs paper (light), 5.74:1 vs paper (dark) — both clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 for text, verified 2026-09-04.

paper-grid.contrastNote: Not a text/UI contrast pair — a 28px repeating-linear-gradient grid on the body background, same ink/cream base as rule-dashed at a much lower 5% alpha, giving the whole page a faint graph-paper texture instead of a flat paper fill.

sealing-wax.contrastNote: 4.66:1 vs paper (light), 6.35:1 vs paper (dark) — the light-mode value was darkened from the initial #ee5a35 (2.85:1, failed as text) to #bc3a14 while staying visibly coral rather than brick; verified 2026-09-04.

display.purpose: Every classification name and heading, always uppercase — the site brand, Explore row names, detail panel name, quiz question/result. The brand's "Classified" line runs very large (clamp(4.4rem, 14vw, 9rem)) so it reads as the first viewport's actual headline; "Type" sits above it as a small eyebrow (clamp(1.4rem, 4vw, 2.6rem)), an asymmetric two-line lockup rather than one uniform brand size.

title.purpose: Section intros and the same oversized-uppercase treatment as display, at a slightly narrower size range for secondary headings.

body.purpose: Running prose — descriptions, taglines, hints — plus the rotated tab labels.

mono.purpose: Anything measured: indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, branch tags, footer credits, timeline marks. A number set in this face reads as data, not prose.

specimen.purpose: A classification's own verified period-accurate typeface for its live 'Aa Gg Qy' and anatomy diagram when self-hosted (Coelacanth/Venetian, Tinos/Transitional), overriding the four roles above for that one piece of content.

extensions.typographyScaleNote: display/title/body/mono above are each one representative size; DESIGN.md's frontmatter typography.scale enumerates the full set of supporting steps (monoXs-monoXxl, bodyXs-bodyXxxxl, titleFluidMin/MaxA/B/C, diagramXs-diagramXxl) that components have actually grown to use, so the design-system checker treats them as a real ramp instead of one-off values.
extensions.shadowNote: This system uses no box-shadow anywhere — see DESIGN.md's 'The Line, Not Light Rule'. Separation between surfaces comes from a 1px border (rule-solid for flush content, ink for floating panels) or a paper/panel tone shift, never blur.

motion.name: ease-cut
motion.purpose: Every state change (view fade-in, tooltip/popover appearance, row hover) steps rather than eases — an instant two-or-three-frame cut instead of a smooth curve, matching the system's printed/mechanical register.

motion.name: bar-draw-in
motion.purpose: The Timeline chart's one authored focal entrance: bars sweep from zero to their true width the first time the Timeline tab is opened (not on every tab switch), via a CSS class scaling the bar to scaleX(0) from its own left edge (transform-box:fill-box) that's removed on that first open. transform, not width, keeps this compositor-only rather than triggering layout. Fully skipped (not shortened) under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Brand tagline switches from right-aligned to left-aligned and drops its max-width.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Tab row gap tightens for small phones.

components.name: Tab
components.description: Rotated vertical label riding a dashed grid rule — the header's view switcher. Per explicit request ('explore, identify, timeline etc be in orange'), the label is sealing-wax colored at all times; inactive/hover/active states are differentiated by opacity (0.6/0.85/1), not by switching between neutral and accent color.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 2rem; height: 78px; align-items: flex-end; border-bottom: 1px solid #d3dbd8; } .ds-tab { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; height: 100%; background: none; border: none; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab-rule { flex: 1; width: 0; border-left: 1px dashed #4d6a67; } .ds-tab-label { writing-mode: vertical-rl; transform: rotate(180deg); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #bc3a14; opacity: 0.6; margin-top: 0.5rem; } .ds-tab--active .ds-tab-rule { border-left-style: solid; border-left-color: #bc3a14; border-left-width: 2px; } .ds-tab--active .ds-tab-label { opacity: 1; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Branch filter above the Explore list and the Compare picker. A solid white (panel) fill rather than transparent, so each chip reads as a distinct element against the cream paper page.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-chip { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #2e5c59; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #004643; border-radius: 0; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #bc3a14; color: #bc3a14; } .ds-chip--active { background: #004643; border-color: #004643; color: #f0ede5; }

components.name: Branch Tag
components.description: Classification-branch mark: a 7px sealing-wax marker square before plain ink-soft text, no box/border/fill. Third revision — a transparent outline read as too faint, a bordered+tinted box read as a heavy UI badge ('looks like a slob'); the marker square gives a legible color cue without the tag reading as a button.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #2e5c59; } .ds-tag::before { content: ""; width: 7px; height: 7px; background: #bc3a14; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Spec Row
components.description: Explore-list row: index, oversized display name, live specimen (set in the classification's own verified font), tagline, era, branch tag.
components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 1.25rem; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: none; border: none; border-top: 1px solid #d3dbd8; padding: 1rem 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-row:hover { background: #ffffff; } .ds-row-index { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; color: #4d6a67; width: 24px; flex-shrink: 0; padding-top: 0.4em; } .ds-row-main { flex: 1; } .ds-row-name { display: block; font-family: Anton, sans-serif; font-size: 2rem; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1; color: #004643; } .ds-row-specimen { display: block; margin-top: 0.4rem; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.5rem; color: #2e5c59; } .ds-row-tagline { display: block; margin-top: 0.3rem; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; color: #2e5c59; } .ds-row-meta { flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-row-era { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; color: #4d6a67; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: The "try your own text" custom specimen field.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Type or paste a word…" />
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem; border: 1px solid #d3dbd8; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #004643; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #4d6a67; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #004643; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #4d6a67; }

components.name: Floating Panel
components.description: The detail modal and quiz card shell — no shadow; separation from the page comes entirely from the solid ink border.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #004643; border-radius: 0; padding: 2rem; max-width: 640px; } .ds-panel-era { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; color: #4d6a67; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-panel-name { font-family: Anton, sans-serif; font-size: 2.4rem; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 0.95; margin-top: 0.35rem; color: #004643; }

components.name: Anatomy Leader-Line
components.description: Signature component: the dashed cap-line/mean-line/baseline annotation, the system's structural idiom extended app-wide.
components.html: <svg width="280" height="90" viewBox="0 0 280 90"><line x1="0" y1="10" x2="280" y2="10" stroke="#4d6a67" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="0" y="7" font-family="JetBrains Mono" font-size="8" fill="#4d6a67">CAP LINE</text><text x="10" y="70" font-family="Anton" font-size="48" fill="#004643">Aa</text><line x1="0" y1="75" x2="280" y2="75" stroke="#4d6a67" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><text x="0" y="72" font-family="JetBrains Mono" font-size="8" fill="#4d6a67">BASELINE</text></svg>

components.name: Timeline Bar
components.description: Signature component: classification bars in flat accent-coral over a chronological teal-to-coral era-band arc, square corners, dashed gridlines. Bars draw themselves in on first reveal (bar-draw-in motion token); era labels scale with era duration; hovering a row label or a bar highlights that pair and dims the rest.
components.html: <svg width="320" height="70" viewBox="0 0 320 70"><rect x="0" y="10" width="320" height="50" fill="rgba(0,70,67,0.35)" /><line x1="160" y1="10" x2="160" y2="60" stroke="rgba(0,70,67,0.22)" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/><rect x="40" y="22" width="200" height="18" rx="0" fill="#bc3a14" /><text x="48" y="34" font-family="JetBrains Mono" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#ffffff">1150 – 1500</text></svg>
components.css: text { letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .tl-bar { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: left center; transition: filter 0.15s ease, transform 0.55s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), opacity 0.15s ease; } .tl-bar.tl-bar--enter { transform: scaleX(0); } .timeline-frozen-wrap.is-hovering .tl-row { opacity: 0.35; } .timeline-frozen-wrap.is-hovering .tl-row.tl-row--highlight { opacity: 1; }

narrative.overview:
Type Classified reads as a technical reference, not a book: a page built like a measured drawing, where a dashed rule and a leader line prove a claim instead of decorating it. This replaced an earlier 'Specimen Ledger' identity (warm parchment, a serif display face, soft ambient shadows) at the user's explicit direction, pinned to two references — a portfolio built from massive stacked client names, and the Cooper Hewitt Museum's 'Type Culture Now' poster, with its dashed vertical grid and rotated section labels — translated onto a white ground instead of the originals' black.

The palette has since moved three times. (1) Corrected to a genuinely neutral grey after reading as too muted: paper #e6e6e6, accent #a8391f -> #c22400 light / #d9714a -> #ff5a33 dark. (2) Ported to warm cream-and-near-black, referencing a font-marketplace specimen sheet: paper #e6e6e6 -> #f3e9dc light / #161616 -> #191510 dark, accent #c22400 -> #bc3a14 light (darkened from the reference's brighter #ee5a35, which measured only 2.85:1 as text) / #ff5a33 -> #f2743f dark. (3) Ported again to deep pine teal and cream, referencing a 'muzudesigns' two-tone font/color card, with the user explicitly choosing to keep a coral third note rather than go fully two-tone ('a dash of orange is good'): paper #f3e9dc -> #f0ede5 light / #191510 -> #004643 dark, ink #1a1611 -> #004643 light / #f3e9dc -> #f0ede5 dark (light and dark mode now literally swap the two reference colors), accent unchanged #bc3a14 light / #f2743f -> #ffb27f dark (lifted further since the dark paper is no longer near-black). The brand headline was also enlarged substantially (clamp(2.4rem,7vw,4rem) -> clamp(3.4rem,11vw,7rem)) so it functions as the first viewport's actual headline, and per explicit request the header tab labels (Explore/Identify/Timeline/Compare) now run in the accent color at all times, differentiated by opacity rather than switching colors; the 'Explore the Classifications' style section headings also gained looser letter-spacing (0.025em) after reading as cramped against the new palette. Branch tags went through three revisions: a transparent outline (too faint), a bordered box with a tint fill ("looks like a slob" — too heavy, read as a UI badge), and finally a small marker square beside plain text. A header graphic (dimension-line SVG) was tried and then removed entirely as clutter.

Every classification name is set in a single oversized condensed grotesque, uppercase, carrying the page the way a poster's headline carries a spread. Everything measured — indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, dimension callouts — is set in a monospace, because a number in a monospace face reads as data, not prose. Corners are square throughout and nothing casts a shadow — separation between surfaces comes from a rule line or a change in tone, never blur.
keyCharacteristics: Cream ground in light mode, deep pine teal in dark mode — the two colors literally swap roles between themes
One condensed display face (Anton) carries every name and headline, always uppercase, at a deliberately large scale
A monospace face marks anything measured: indices, dates, dimensions, tags
Dashed rules are structural, not decorative — they mark a grid, a leader line, a boundary
Square corners everywhere; separation comes from a rule or a tone change, never a shadow
Coral-orange marks small things and the whole tab-label system — a marker square on every tag, bars, measurement call-outs, and every tab label (opacity-differentiated, not color-differentiated)

rules.name: The Small Mark Rule
rules.body: Sealing Wax never fills a surface larger than a 7px marker square, a 2px border, or a bar on the timeline. A branch tag's own text stays ink-soft, not accent — the color lives in the marker, not the label. Tab labels are the one exception: their text is accent-colored at all times, differentiated by opacity rather than switching colors, per explicit request.

rules.name: The Teal-and-Cream Rule
rules.body: Every 'ink' step is a shade of deep pine teal, every 'paper' step a shade of cream — and in dark mode, teal and cream swap roles entirely, mirroring the reference's own two panels. This is the palette's third distinct direction this session; if it moves a fourth time, make the choice deliberately rather than drifting again.

rules.name: The One Voice, One Data Rule
rules.body: Anton names things; Inter explains things; JetBrains Mono measures things. No role ever borrows another's job.

rules.name: The Line, Not Light Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow appears anywhere in this system. A surface separates from the page behind it with a border or a tone change; if neither reads clearly enough, the surface's content or size is wrong, not its shadow.

dos: Do set every classification name and heading in Anton, uppercase, at large scale.
Do set anything measured (an index, a date, a diagnostic, a dimension) in JetBrains Mono.
Do separate every surface with a border or a tone shift, never a shadow.
Do keep Sealing Wax to a marker square on tags, bars, and measurement marks — bright, but still small.
donts: Don't reintroduce a shadow anywhere, however soft.
Don't round a corner. border-radius: 0 is absolute, no exceptions — including SVG geometry.
Don't drift the neutrals' hue/warmth without a deliberate decision — this palette has already moved three times (neutral grey -> warm cream/near-black -> teal/cream).

Don't ship a font whose classification lineage is wrong for the sake of a better-looking specimen — the live Aa Gg Qy specimens still render in each classification's own verified typeface beneath the new Anton display name, not replaced by it.
